    Parents, children and arms in a finite tree #

    Proof of Proposition 4.1, Step 2: "The tree is consequently a path or has one trivalent vertex. In the latter case let p ≤ q ≤ r be its arm lengths."

    Seen from a root o, each other vertex has a unique parent (TreeBFS); its other neighbours are its children. This file sets up parents, children and ancestors.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

                            Proposition 4.1, Step 2: the tree is Dynkin. A finite tree carrying a vector n > 0 with Mn > 0 is a star with at most one arm (a path rooted at an end) or with three arms satisfying ∑ p_i/(p_i + 1) < 2.
